question: Can the existing Wingless raw-byte substrate build a second learned granularity level on real UTF-8 prose/code bytes and preserve predictive/efficiency gains on a fresh immutable cross-file holdout without tokenization?
hypothesis: On the frozen larger real-byte corpus, a fixed hierarchy of 512 four-byte motifs plus 128 eight-byte compounds formed only from adjacent selected motifs will cover at least 8% of held-out positions at level 1 and at least 0.5% at level 2, improve next-byte accuracy by at least 0.05 over the level-1 predictor on level-2-covered positions, reduce effective held-out events by at least 0.12, and not worsen bits-per-byte relative to the level-1 model.
authority: research-only real-byte hierarchy pilot; no deployment or external-model inference authority

corpus.encoding: exact Git blob bytes; no UTF decoding, normalization, tokenizer, subword vocabulary, boundary tokens, or remapping
corpus.file_boundary_policy: reset byte context/hierarchy scan at every file boundary
corpus.contamination_rule: No eval blob may appear in training. Every blob identity must match before model construction.

learner.baseline: fixed 256x256 previous-byte -> next-byte uint32 counts; lowest-byte argmax tie break; Jeffreys categorical smoothing

level1.candidate: every raw four-byte training window with following byte
level1.score: best-successor count descending, then best-successor fraction descending, then lexicographic raw key
level1.state: four-byte key plus 256 successor uint32 counts

level2.candidate: an eight-byte training span whose first four bytes and second four bytes are both exact selected level-1 motif keys; candidate has following raw byte
level2.score: best-successor count descending, then best-successor fraction descending, then lexicographic eight-byte key
level2.state: eight-byte key plus 256 successor uint32 counts
level2.forbidden: no level2 candidate may form unless both component halves were independently selected at level1

learner.prediction: longest learned context wins: level2 eight-byte distribution, else level1 four-byte distribution, else baseline one-byte distribution
learner.probability: Jeffreys-smoothed categorical probability (count+0.5)/(context_total+128) at the selected hierarchy level

controls.level1_only: same baseline and selected 512 level1 motifs with level2 disabled
controls.baseline_only: same previous-byte baseline with both motif levels disabled

evaluation.level1_coverage: fraction of positions with at least four prior bytes whose last four bytes match a selected level1 motif
evaluation.level2_coverage: fraction of positions with at least eight prior bytes whose last eight bytes match a selected level2 compound
evaluation.level2_accuracy_gain: hierarchical top-1 accuracy minus level1-only top-1 accuracy restricted to level2-covered positions
evaluation.event_reduction: greedy raw scan: selected level2 span consumes 8 bytes as one event; else selected level1 span consumes 4 bytes as one event; else one raw byte event
evaluation.bpb: mean negative log2 smoothed probability per next byte; report hierarchical minus level1 and hierarchical minus baseline per eval file

validity_criteria: Exact parent and North Star identity match.
All Git blob identities match and train/eval blob sets are disjoint.
The learner receives exact raw bytes only and resets state at file boundaries.
Every level2 key is exactly eight raw bytes composed of two selected adjacent level1 keys.
No eval bytes participate in candidate selection or learned counts.
Fixed capacities are 512 level1 plus 128 level2; no capacity growth.
Full Go regression passes before probe execution.
Normalized result carries the exact experiment identifier.

classification_rules.supported: All frozen thresholds and validity criteria pass.
classification_rules.mixed: Level2 forms and improves either prediction or event efficiency but at least one coverage/BPB threshold fails.
classification_rules.negative: Validity passes but level2 provides no held-out predictive/efficiency advantage over the level1-only control.
classification_rules.incomplete: Corpus or compute interruption prevents complete evaluation.
classification_rules.invalid: Blob identity, train/eval isolation, raw-byte identity, hierarchy construction, capacity, determinism, or qualification criteria fail.

no_post_result_tuning_rule: Do not change corpus blobs, capacities, minimum counts, scoring, smoothing, prediction precedence, metrics, thresholds, or classification after observing output.
